newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes steady late, sours plummet on SPR sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes steady late, sours plummet on SPR sale.

text.p: U.S. crudes rounded out afternoon trading on a steady note, while sour grades sank under the weight of the latest crude sales from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) and fundamental pressures.
Outright prices came under pressure over the day following the NYMEX on reports that the U.S. was edging toward accepting the Iraqi pricing formula under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $23.70-80 a barrel, about steady with Wednesday's late cash market.
The Dec/Jan WTI spread was around 10 cents, with two deals confirmed at five cents and 13 cents.
Dec Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was was in the range of 72-80 cents over WTI/Cushing, with three deals done at 76/85/88 cents over the day, down a few cents from Wednesday.
Heavy Lousiana Sweet/Empire picked up steam in the afternoon, with three deals done at 35/45/50 cts over WTI, about steady with Wednesday.
The closed trans-Atlantic arbitrage has boosted refiner demand for sweet grades, although LLS came off highs of $1.10 Wednesday as some refiners sought to optimize runs by turning to sour grades.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded as low as WTI minus $2.20 in the afternoon, before recovering to a range of minus $2.10-1.90, down 20 cents from Wednesday.

The U.S. government sold 1.075 million barrels of sour crude from the SPR to three refiners for an average price of $21.33 a barrel as part of plan to raise revenue. The sales have put continuing pressure on U.S. sour grades.
